**Synopsis:**
European central bankers are leaving the 2026 Jackson Hole symposium deeply unsettled about the trajectory of US policy and global financial cooperation. Key concerns: (1) The US Treasury sold euros to buy yen without giving Europe a customary heads-up; (2) Bessent's long-end bond buyback program is seen as a stealth attempt to suppress long yields, blurring the line between fiscal and monetary policy; (3) There is latent fear that Trump could weaponize or disrupt Fed dollar swap lines used as global liquidity backstops. Fed officials (under new Chair Kevin Warsh) are trying to reassure allies but cannot guarantee against further unilateral White House actions. The overarching narrative is one of eroding trust in US multilateral norms, with Europe worried about escalating and unpredictable US interventionism.
